title: King Oliver
summary: Bunn heard Joe Oliver play but did not sit in with his groups.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Uh-huh. I wanted to try and go back again, back to the '30s, and talk about some of the different people you worked with.
Yeah.

In the recording sessions. And just take them up one at a time, and anything you could remember would be helpful. You know, whether it's a personal comment or musical or whatever, you know. For example, yesterday I asked you if you'd ever run into Joe Oliver in the old days.
Yeah.
And I wonder if you remember anything about him.
No. All I know is he played all right to me.
Uh-huh.
The way he played to me was all right with me at that time. As I got older and the music commenced to get older, it sounded a little different, but every time I'd hear him, he sounded the same.
Uh-huh. Did you ever --
He didn't do too much changing it.
He had his thing and he --
Yeah, he had his thing going and he kept it going.
Did you ever sit in with any of his groups?
Huh?
Did you ever sit in with any of his groups?
Who, Joe Oliver?
Yeah.
No.
No.
Not as that I remember.
You just heard him in the --
Yeah.
-- the ballrooms or whatever.
Not as that I remember. I might have, I don't know.
Oh, yeah. Well --
It was coming so fast for me, too.
